Schema: `agency_members` + `name`/`email` (team directory copy; `users` stays app_auth-only) + `deactivated_at`; STRICT `agency_invites` (email, role, inviter, locale, HMAC token set by the email job, 7-day expiry, single use, one open invite per email). Migrations 0007 (tables + backfill with FORCE RLS lifted per table), 0008 + 0009 guard triggers: app_user never inserts/deletes members, changes only role/deactivation, only as an active admin, never on its own row, only within its role family; invites only by an active admin (open, tokenless, own family), tenant sessions only revoke; app_auth only marks an open invite accepted by the scoped user. Registry: `agency_invites` `auth` predicates, `agency_members` insert also allowed for a user who accepted an invite of that agency for that role, new `guardedInsert` flag + isolation-suite branch. Service: `listMembers`/`listInvites` (keyset, ≤ 100), `inviteMember` (`ALREADY_MEMBER`; re-invite replaces; unverified agencies ≤ 5 seats → `VERIFICATION_REQUIRED`; `billing.assertSeat` stub), `revokeInvite`, `changeMemberRole`, `deactivateMember` (both lock caller + target rows in id order, revoke the target's sent invites when they stop being an admin), `acceptInvite` (anonymous; token = agency id hex + random; creates a confirmed account and the membership in one tx; `TOKEN_INVALID` / `INVITE_EMAIL_IN_USE`). Login, `isSessionValid`, `issueAccessToken` and `withMemberCtx` refuse deactivated members. Sign-up L3: a repeat sign-up replaces the password only together with an untouched (PENDING, not onboarded) agency, else "account exists" email. `identity.sendInviteEmail` job (EN/ES; skips if the inviter is no longer an active admin). API: `GET /v1/members`, `PUT /v1/members/:userId/role`, `POST /v1/members/:userId/deactivate`, `GET/POST /v1/invites`, `DELETE /v1/invites/:inviteId` (invite: + per-tenant 100/h, per-user 50/day). Web: `/accept-invite` (no-referrer), `/team` page (EN/ES), login "joined" notice. New `billing` module (stub), `core/pagination.ts`, `contracts/common.ts`. Tests: team int 16, identity policy 4, api int 1 new, isolation (guardedInsert branch + `agency_invites`). code-reviewer + security-auditor must-fixes fixed; rest under Decisions. ## Decisions

- 2026-10-10 · **Node.js 24 LTS** for dev and CI; production servers support 22 and 24, so root `engines.node` is `>=22 <25`. Record in ADR 0001. PLAN §5.8 updated. (Shahzaib)
- 2026-10-10 · **PostgreSQL 17+** (PLAN §5.1 said 16; §5.8, S0-02 and PATTERNS §13 `MERGE … RETURNING merge_action()` need 17). §5.1 corrected.
- 2026-10-10 · **Next.js latest stable** (PLAN §5.2 said 15; §5.8 says latest stable). §5.2 corrected; exact version pinned in ADR 0001.
- 2026-10-10 · **Email and storage adapters** have no S0 task. Build `platform/email` (Resend/SES drivers, Mailpit locally) inside S0-09, and `platform/storage` (R2/MinIO, private buckets, signed URLs) inside S1-03, both following the platform adapter pattern. (Shahzaib approved)
- 2026-10-10 · **Forward dependencies:** S3-10 depends on S4-02, and S5-06 depends on S11-04. S3 and S5 can close with those two tasks marked `BLOCKED S4-02` / `BLOCKED S11-04`; each task finishes when its dependency is DONE.
- 2026-10-10 · Repo path is `E:\Repos\InmolinkCRM` (docs said `E:\Repos\Inmolink`; PLAN §22 and BUILD-GUIDE fixed). Remote: `https://github.com/gr8xpert/Inmolink-CRM.git`.
- 2026-10-10 · **TypeScript 6.0.3, not 7.0** (S0-01). TS 7 has no JS compiler API yet, and Next API-mode type checking, dependency-cruiser, SDK codegen and tsdown d.ts depend on it. Revisit at each sprint review (ADR 0001).
- 2026-10-10 · **pnpm 10.33.2 pinned, pnpm 12 deferred** (S0-01). pnpm 10's auto-switch to `pnpm@12.10.1` fails on this machine because the user path contains a space (`Shah PC`). Upgrade after installing pnpm 12 globally (ADR 0001).
- 2026-10-10 · **Package exports use a `@inmolink/source` condition** (S0-01). Typecheck, Vitest and tsx resolve TypeScript source; builds and Next resolve tsdown `dist/`. App packages are named `@inmolink/app-<name>`. `apps/wp-plugin` stays outside the pnpm workspace (PHP tooling).
- 2026-10-10 · **Stubbed root scripts exit 1** with the owning task ID, so nothing silently pretends to work. `verify` gains `check:boundaries` (S0-12) and `test:isolation` (S0-05) when those tasks land.
- 2026-10-10 · **PostgreSQL 18** (S0-02). PG 18.6 is the newest major with PostGIS 3.6, pgvector 0.8.7 and pg_partman 5.5 all packaged (PGDG), within "17+". Image `inmolink/postgres:18-3.6` is built from `postgis/postgis:18-3.6`. Production must run the same major (S0-15).
- 2026-10-10 · **MinIO image from `pgsty/minio`** (S0-02). Upstream MinIO stopped publishing Docker images; `pgsty/minio` and `pgsty/mc` are the community builds of the same server and client. Local/CI only — production storage is R2. If that fork stalls, swap to any S3-compatible server; the storage adapter (S1-03) only speaks S3.
- 2026-10-10 · **`pnpm verify` needs Docker** (S0-02). Root `test:int:root` (tests/infra) runs in `verify` and its global setup runs `docker compose --profile test up -d --wait`. Package integration tests from S0-04 on use the same test stack. The stack stays up between runs; `pnpm infra:down` stops both profiles.
- 2026-10-10 · **Bootstrap superuser `postgres` is for ops only** (S0-02). `DATABASE_URL_ADMIN(_POOLED)` serve health checks and scripts. App roles (`app_owner`, `app_user`, `app_system`, `app_public`) are created in S0-04. PgBouncer finds them through `auth_query`, so S0-04 does not need to edit `userlist.txt`.
- 2026-10-10 · **pg and ioredis were added in S0-02**, earlier than planned, for the health script. Versions match ADR 0001: pg 8.23.1 and ioredis 6.0.0. ioredis 6 defaults to RESP3, and the health script passes `protocol: 2`. S0-06 must choose the protocol on purpose for BullMQ.
- 2026-10-10 · **Outbox is a STRICT, append-only tenant table** (S0-06). Request transactions insert their own agency's events (RLS `for insert`, INSERT-only grant); platform-wide events use the nil UUID and only `withSystem()` can write them. The dispatcher and replay read/ack via `withSystem()`. The registry gained `appendOnly` (PATTERNS §2).
- 2026-10-10 · **`@inmolink/platform` does not depend on `@inmolink/db`** (S0-06): `emit` takes a structural `SqlExecutor`; the dispatcher gets `runSystem` (= `withSystem`) and `listen` injected. The table schema lives in `packages/db/src/schema/outbox.ts`, the SQL in platform/outbox (column names kept in sync, covered by the int tests). Outbox/queue integration tests live at the root (`tests/queue`, `tests/perf`) because the root depends on both.
- 2026-10-10 · **LISTEN needs a direct connection** (S0-06): PgBouncer transaction mode cannot hold LISTEN, so `DATABASE_URL_LISTEN` (optional, workers only, refused for APP_ROLE=http in production; `listen()` also calls `assertSystemAllowed()`) points straight at Postgres. It uses the `app_system` credential today; a dedicated no-grant `app_listen` login role is a follow-up for S0-15 (security audit). Without it the dispatcher polls (1 s).
- 2026-10-10 · **Fair share on open-source BullMQ** (S0-06): BullMQ groups are Pro-only, so `platform/queue/fairness.ts` sets priority = the group's backlog depth (interleaves groups) and enforces `concurrencyPerGroup` with a Lua lease set (a job that finds its group full goes back to delayed). Jobs without `group` keep priority 0 and run before grouped ones — give every tenant-scoped job a group. The batched script spans many keys, so redis-queue must stay a single node (or share a hash-tag prefix).
- 2026-10-10 · **ioredis protocol 2 for BullMQ** (S0-06, resolves the S0-02 note): RESP2 pinned on every queue connection. Producer: `maxRetriesPerRequest: 1` + auto-pipelining (an enqueue fails fast, so the dispatcher retries the event instead of stalling); workers: `maxRetriesPerRequest: null` (BullMQ requirement).
- 2026-10-10 · **Throughput check is the best 10 k window** (S0-06). On this Windows + Docker Desktop machine with ~60 % background CPU, single windows vary 1.5–4.7 k ev/s (autovacuum, AOF rewrite, desktop load); overall rates were 2.35–2.9 k in the last runs. The test reports all windows + overall and asserts the best window ≥ 2,000. CI on Linux (S0-14) should assert the overall rate instead. `test:perf:root` runs last in `verify` (turbo `dependsOn`) and restarts the **test** redis-queue with plain `docker restart` (`docker compose restart` drops the published port on Docker Desktop for Windows).
- 2026-10-10 · **Follow-ups from S0-06 reviews (accepted for now):** (1) the outbox claim is global FIFO — one agency's 100 k-event import delays other agencies' events; add a per-agency cap per claim before R2 imports (jobs downstream already have fair share). (2) `emit` sends NOTIFY, which serializes commits of notifying transactions on a global lock; measure with many concurrent emitters before R2 imports and drop NOTIFY for polling if it shows. (3) every dispatcher poll writes a `withSystem` audit log line; give routine system queries a quieter audit level in S0-10. (4) `last_error` and DLQ entries keep raw error text — tenants cannot read either (outbox is INSERT-only for app_user; the DLQ is Redis, ops only). (5) no DLQ re-enqueue tool yet; add it with the ops runbook (S0-15).
- 2026-10-10 · **Feature flag overrides live on the global `feature_flags` row** (S0-07) as `enabled_for`/`disabled_for` agency ID arrays, not a STRICT per-agency table: a STRICT table would let `app_user` switch its own agency's flags on. Consequences, accepted: any `app_user` session can read which agency IDs are on a pilot (no endpoint exposes rows; `flag()` returns a boolean for `ctx.tenant` only — never return raw rows to tenants, keep descriptions free of customer names); flags are **dashboard/worker only** (`app_public` has no grant; feed-api would need a deliberate `publicRead` or a read model). Writes have no audit entry yet — add one with the staff UI (who, why, old/new).
- 2026-10-10 · **Rate-limit counters share redis-cache** (S0-07, allkeys-lru): eviction under memory pressure can reset a counter, and non-credential rules fail open when Redis is down (PLAN §5.4 degrade). Credential rules (`auth.*`, `password.*`, `2fa.*`) are forced to fail closed. If cache pressure is ever seen evicting auth counters, move them to a small `volatile-lru` Redis DB (S0-15). Windows use the app server clock (NTP-synced), not Redis `TIME` — skew only loosens a limit slightly.
- 2026-10-10 · **Cache single-flight is per process** (S0-07): N app processes can run the loader N times on a cold key; no distributed lock (accepted — bounded by node count). Other processes' in-process (`local`) copies and flag snapshots expire within 60 s of an invalidation.
- 2026-10-10 · **PATTERNS §15 changed** (S0-07): keys are built with `cacheKey()` (branded `CacheKey`; `get`/`set`/`delete` accept nothing else), adding a mandatory scope segment (`g` or `a.<agencyId>`) and tagged id/locale/view segments; rate-limit and flag usage added. Reason: security audit — an untenanted key plus single-flight would serve one agency's RLS-scoped result to another.
- 2026-10-10 · **Windows test-run instability, open** (S0-07): (1) vitest fork workers intermittently die with exit 0xC0000409 (native abort, no stderr) in int/perf files — ~2 in 20 runs on this machine, seen in pre-existing S0-06 files as well as new ones; a re-run passes. Not reproduced on HEAD in 8 runs, which is not conclusive. Mitigations: `adapters` files run serially and after `infra`+`queue`. Re-check on Linux CI (S0-14); if it persists, try `pool: 'threads'` for the int projects. (2) the S0-06 perf test's `docker restart` of redis-queue-test can come back **without its published port** on Docker Desktop, after which every queue test fails to reach Redis; `restartRedisQueue()` now checks `docker port` and recreates the container (same AOF volume) when the port is missing. Prior test runs also leave large AOF files in redis-queue-test (5.5 s load); `pnpm infra:down` + volume prune resets it.
- 2026-10-10 · **Boundary rule for apps is "core / contracts / platform / ui"** (S0-08). PATTERNS §11 already imports platform from apps; S0-12's text says "core/contracts/ui only". Apps reach the database only through `@inmolink/core` (`configureDb`, `closeDb`, `pingDb`, `withRequestCtx`, `createOutboxDispatcher`, re-exported in `core/src/runtime.ts`). Exception: app **tests** may import `@inmolink/db/testing` (devDependency) to bring the test stack up. S0-12's dependency-cruiser rules must encode exactly this.
- 2026-10-10 · **Shared Fastify plumbing is `@inmolink/platform/server`** (S0-08), not a new package: it is infrastructure (rule 10), and platform already peers on fastify for the rate-limit plugin. `@fastify/type-provider-zod` 1.0.0 (the official successor of `fastify-type-provider-zod`) and `@fastify/swagger` are platform dependencies; Swagger UI is imported only when `/docs` is on.
- 2026-10-10 · **Each deployable pins `APP_ROLE` in code** (S0-08): api/feed-api/realtime → `http`, worker → `worker`; the env value is ignored. feed-api loads only `DATABASE_URL_APP_PUBLIC` and `REDIS_CACHE_URL` (no queue); api/realtime only `DATABASE_URL_APP_USER`. `DbConfig` role URLs became optional, so a process cannot open a pool it was not given.
- 2026-10-10 · **next-intl is wired in S0-11, not S0-08** (S0-08). S0-11 owns `packages/i18n`, the locale config and locale-prefixed routing; a partial setup now would hard-code a locale. S0-08 ships Tailwind v4 + shadcn base and `/healthz` for both Next apps; `<html lang>` is fixed to `en` until then.
- 2026-10-10 · **Next dev ports 3100 (web) / 3101 (public)** (S0-08): ports 3000–3002 are taken by another local project (the Inmolink marketplace) on this machine. Fastify apps: api 4000, feed-api 4001, realtime 4002, worker health 4003.
- 2026-10-10 · **App runtimes need a real `.env`** (S0-08, security audit): `loadStackEnv('dev', { allowExample: false })`; only `db:migrate` and tests fall back to `*.example`. A container that lost its secrets now fails config validation instead of booting on example keys in development mode. `.env.test.example` gained dev-convention test crypto keys. Exclude `.env*` from images when Dockerfiles land (S0-14/S0-15).
- 2026-10-10 · **`TRUST_PROXY` is strict** (S0-08, security audit): `false`, a hop count 1–3, or a list of keywords/IPs/CIDRs no wider than /8 (IPv4) or /16 (IPv6). `true`, `0.0.0.0/0`, `::/0` and large hop counts are refused, because each would let clients forge `X-Forwarded-For` and reset their rate-limit bucket.
- 2026-10-10 · **Request-path apps do not get the Meilisearch master key** (S0-08, security audit): api and feed-api load only `MEILI_URL` (readiness). The search adapter task brings a scoped search key; the master key stays with the worker's indexing pool and scripts.
- 2026-10-10 · **Graceful shutdown order** (S0-08): `draining` (readiness 503) → optional `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_DELAY_MS` (default 0; kamal-proxy drains on its own) → `closing` (new requests 503 with `Connection: close`) → `app.close()` waits for in-flight requests → queues/cache/db close. Worker pools get 25 s inside the 30 s process deadline, then stalled jobs are retried. Next apps rely on `next start`'s own SIGTERM handling. On Windows, SIGTERM cannot be delivered to a child process, so the boot test asserts exit 0 only on Linux; the drain itself is tested in-process.
- 2026-10-10 · **Realtime pub/sub runs on redis-cache** (S0-08) through `pubSubConnections()` from platform/cache: pub/sub stores no keys, so allkeys-lru is harmless, and redis-queue stays dedicated to jobs. Move it to its own instance if realtime traffic ever crowds the cache node.
- 2026-10-10 · **Follow-ups from S0-08 reviews (accepted for now):** (1) the "Postgres down behind PgBouncer" hang is covered by a fake hung check plus a manual dev run (503 in ~2 s), not an automated test against PgBouncer. (2) The worker health server shares `HOST`; give it a private bind (`WORKER_HEALTH_HOST`) in S0-15. (3) `/readyz` names its dependencies in public responses (ok/fail only; reasons are logged); hide `checks` at the edge if that matters. (4) The tests deliver SIGTERM with `process.emit`, which would also reach any vitest SIGTERM listener; stable so far. (5) The `apps` test project runs in the `threads` pool after a fork worker crashed with 0xC0000409 under full-suite load (the open Windows issue from S0-07).
- 2026-10-10 · **Proposed ADR 0004 — new login role `app_auth`** (S0-09, extends PLAN §3 #30/#50; review at the S0 sprint review). Login runs before a tenant is known and staff have no agency, so `users`/`auth_tokens` are global tables (`access: 'auth'`) reachable only by `app_auth` (select/insert/update) and `app_system`; `app_user` cannot read password hashes. `app_auth` may append outbox rows only with the nil agency and `type` starting `identity.`. Needs `DATABASE_URL_APP_AUTH` per environment (only `web` uses it).
- 2026-10-10 · **Auth flows run in `web`, calling core directly** (S0-09). Auth.js must verify credentials server-side, so the auth server actions, `authorize()` and `/session/token` call `@inmolink/core/modules/identity` through `AuthCtx` (`withAuth`). frontend.md now names this as the only exception to "web talks to api"; tenant data still goes through the API. Web has no socket IP: `clientIpFromForwarded` applies the same `TRUST_PROXY` model to `X-Forwarded-For`, and web refuses `TRUST_PROXY=false` in production.
- 2026-10-10 · **Auth.js `5.0.0-beta.32`** (S0-09): PLAN says Auth.js v5; the v5 line is still published as beta (peer range covers Next 16). Pinned exactly. Revisit when v5 goes stable.
- 2026-10-10 · **Access tokens: Ed25519, 15 min, per audience** (S0-09): web signs, api/realtime verify with public keys (`AUTH_JWT_PUBLIC_KEYS=kid:spki,…`). No per-request DB check in the API; revocation = no new tokens after a password reset (`session_version`), so a stolen token lives ≤ 15 min. Web sessions re-check the user every 5 min (Auth.js `jwt` callback) and end when revoked. Logout clears the cookie only; "log out everywhere" (bump `session_version`) comes with session management (S1-02).
- 2026-10-10 · **Email confirmation needs the account password** (S0-09, security audit M1): prevents pre-account hijack (someone signs up with another person's address and the owner confirms it). A repeat sign-up on an unconfirmed email replaces that pending account and re-sends the link. Display names reject links (no `://`, dots must be followed by a space) because they appear in our emails.
- 2026-10-10 · **Login limits** (S0-09, review): per IP 30/15 min, per email+IP 10/15 min, per email 100/h (distributed-guessing ceiling), all fail closed; sign-up per IP 10/h and per email 3/h; reset requests per IP 10/h and per email 3/h. Per-email-only limits would let anyone lock an owner out; the email+IP key avoids that. Values are working figures.
- 2026-10-10 · **Auth forms use `useActionState` + server-side Zod** (S0-09), not react-hook-form: the forms work without JavaScript and errors come back by code. Pages pick EN/ES from `Accept-Language` and use the interim `translator()` from `@inmolink/i18n`; S0-11 moves them to next-intl and locale-prefixed routes.
- 2026-10-10 · **`loadStackEnv` finds the repo root by walking up from the working directory** (S0-09): Next bundles workspace packages, so `import.meta.dirname` is undefined there.
- 2026-10-10 · **Follow-ups from S0-09 reviews (accepted for now):** (1) Turnstile on sign-up and forgot-password (PLAN §12) — needs site keys; add with the edge work (S0-15) or as a human action. (2) `auth_tokens` retention: a maintenance job deleting rows used/expired > 7 days, with an index on `expires_at`. (3) `users.email` is lower-cased only by the contract; add `check (email = lower(email))` when identity next changes. (4) Realtime auth covers the default namespace only; S11 must apply the same middleware to `/chat` and `/notifications` (`io.of(/.*/).use`). (5) `/session/expired` signs out on GET (SameSite=Strict limits it to a same-site nuisance). (6) The API has no CORS yet: the browser does not call it until the typed client lands; add an exact-origin allowlist then. (7) The feed-api boot test got a 30 s timeout after a cold module load exceeded 5 s under full `verify` parallelism.
- 2026-10-10 · **Telemetry is a platform adapter, metrics are scraped** (S0-10, PLAN §3 #44 "OpenTelemetry → Grafana stack"). Traces: OTLP/HTTP to a collector (Jaeger locally; Grafana Tempo or Better Stack in S0-15). Metrics: each app's Prometheus endpoint on a private port (`*_METRICS_PORT`, 0 = off), not OTLP — no extra collector pipeline for metrics. Web (Next) has no `/metrics` yet; its server spans and errors are covered.
- 2026-10-10 · **Sentry for Next.js = server side only** (S0-10): `onRequestError` → the same `reportError` as the Node apps (`@sentry/node`), no `@sentry/nextjs`. The browser SDK (and source-map upload) waits for real client UI and the CI/deploy work (S0-14/S0-15), within the 250 KB dashboard budget. The web process does not flush spans/errors on SIGTERM (Next owns its shutdown).
- 2026-10-10 · **Remote trace context** (S0-10, security audit M1/M2): api, feed-api, realtime and web re-sample an inbound `traceparent` by the ratio (`trustRemoteParent: false`; the trace-id ratio sampler keeps one decision per trace across our services); only W3C trace context is propagated (no baggage); Sentry's Http/NodeFetch integrations are removed and `tracePropagationTargets: []`. **For `safeFetch` (feeds, webhooks, images):** run requests to user-supplied URLs under `suppressTracing()` so no `traceparent` reaches third parties.
- 2026-10-10 · **Outbox OTLP transport** (S0-10, audit S4): spans carry SQL text and routes; production must send OTLP to a collector on the private network (or https). Recorded for S0-15.
- 2026-10-10 · **`withSystem(reason, fn, { routine: true })`** logs its audit line at `debug` (S0-06 follow-up 3, done in S0-10); only the outbox dispatcher uses it. Every other `withSystem` call still logs at `info`.
- 2026-10-10 · **`@opentelemetry/api` is a dependency of db and core** (S0-10) only so pnpm resolves one drizzle-orm peer variant (drizzle has an optional peer on it); otherwise drizzle's `SQL` types from two copies clash.
- 2026-10-10 · **Follow-ups from S0-10 reviews (accepted for now):** (1) bulk producers (R2 imports emitting 10 k+ events) should start a new root per delivery with a span link to the emitter instead of a child, or one trace grows without bound. (2) Sample ratio and batch queue (`maxQueueSize` 4,096) need a `/perf-check` at feed-api's 1,000 rps once feed-api has real routes (S1/S2). (3) The `trace_parent` check constraint was added with a plain `ADD CONSTRAINT` (scans the outbox; small, pruned table). (4) **E2E flake:** the S0-09 sign-up test intermittently finds no status after the first "Create account" click on a cold `next dev` (2 of 5 full `pnpm test:e2e` runs; the page re-navigates to `/signup`), passing on rerun; root cause not found — investigate with the Playwright trace before S0-14 makes e2e a CI gate. (5) `pnpm verify` load starves redis-cache commands past the 200 ms cut-off; the web login-limit int test now uses `commandTimeoutMs: 2_000` (new `configureCache` option, default unchanged).
- 2026-10-10 · graphify knowledge-graph hooks live in `.claude/settings.local.json` (machine-specific, not committed); `graphify-out/` is git-ignored.
- 2026-10-10 · **Catalogs are bundled, not read from disk** (S0-11). Turbopack bundles workspace packages even when listed in `serverExternalPackages`, so a runtime `fs` read relative to the module fails the build. `pnpm i18n:draft` writes `packages/i18n/src/catalogs.generated.ts` (static JSON imports of the configured locales); `i18n:check` fails when it is stale. Adding a locale = edit `locales.json` + run `pnpm i18n:draft` + review drafts — no hand-written code.
- 2026-10-10 · **Content locales launch with the six PLAN names (es, en, nl, de, fr, sv)** (S0-11, PLAN §3 #14). The other three of legacy's nine come from the legacy inventory (PLAN §14 step 1) and are a config change. UI locales stay EN + ES (hand-written); others are drafted.
- 2026-10-10 · **Drafted-locale bookkeeping** (S0-11): `messages/<locale>/_drafts.json` maps `namespace → key → todo|draft`; until S12-01 a new key carries the EN text marked `todo` (the "TODO marker"), so drafted locales never show raw keys. A reviewer removes the mark. Hand-written locales (EN, ES) may not have marks and are never written by `i18n:draft`.
- 2026-10-10 · **Locale routing** (S0-11): `localePrefix: 'always'` in both apps (default `en`); `/login`-style links in Auth.js (`pages.signIn`) and `/session/expired` stay unprefixed — the proxy redirects them by the `NEXT_LOCALE` cookie, which is the right locale for a route handler that has none. Web sets `alternateLinks: false` (no hreflang `Link` header that would echo one-time tokens); public keeps it for SEO. Matchers skip only exact `/api`, `/session`, `/healthz` prefixes and paths with a dot — **portal slugs must not contain dots** (S2 slug generator). Root layouts send no catalogs to the client (`messages={null}`); a client subtree that needs strings gets its own provider with only its namespaces.

- 2026-10-11 · **S1-01 agencies and sign-up.**
  - `agencies` keys on `agency_id` (TS `id`), so the registry, RLS and isolation suite need no special case.

Membership predicates also require the agency to be visible to app_auth (PENDING, not onboarded).
  - Functions that build `ctx` take a raw `tx` (`agencies.createSignupAgency`, `agencies.loadTenant`, `identity.getMemberRole`): no `Ctx` exists yet. Not for other use cases.

  - Column-level protection uses guard triggers (migration 0006) instead of column grants, which the RLS guard rejects. S1-02 replaces the member-role trigger.
  - After verification, name and tax id are locked (`AGENCY_DETAILS_LOCKED`). **S1-03 must bind an approval to the details `version` staff reviewed** (a PENDING agency could otherwise change details mid-review).

- 2026-10-11 · **S1-02 users, roles, invites, seats.**
  - **No `session_version` bump on role change or deactivation** (deviates from the S1-01 note). `users` is reachable only by app_auth, so a tenant session cannot bump it. Deactivation is a membership state (`agency_members.deactivated_at`) checked at login (same error as a wrong password), by `isSessionValid` (the web session ends at its next Auth.js re-check, ≤ 5 min), by `issueAccessToken` (no new tokens) and per request by `withMemberCtx` (the API refuses the user on the next call, even with an unexpired token). A role change needs no revocation: the role is read per request.
  - Roles by family: AGENCY_ADMIN manages AGENCY_ADMIN/AGENT, DEVELOPER_ADMIN the developer roles (policy + guard trigger 0009). "Only AGENCY_ADMIN" in the task covers DEVELOPER_ADMIN for developer tenants, as in the agencies policy.
  - Invite token = agency id (32 hex) + random part: the anonymous accept flow pins its app_auth scope to that agency before the HMAC lookup. Accepting creates a confirmed account (the link proves the inbox).
  - An email that already has an account cannot accept (`INVITE_EMAIL_IN_USE`, one agency per user). Known gap (review): an unconfirmed sign-up squatting the email blocks invites; follow-up — let a valid invite take over an unconfirmed, untouched sign-up (S1-F4).
  - `agency_members.name/email` copy `users` at join time; a future profile/email change must update the copy through an event.
  - Seat hook `billing.assertSeat(ctx, { used })` (stub, unlimited) counts active members + open invites; S13 must lock the agency row before counting (two concurrent invites can both pass). Unverified agencies are capped at 5 seats (security review M2), plus invite rate limits per tenant (100/h) and per user (50/day).
  - No `Idempotency-Key` on `POST /v1/invites` (no middleware exists yet): re-inviting an email replaces its open invite, so retries do not duplicate. Add with the idempotency platform work.
  - Migration 0007 backfills `name/email` in-migration (one UPDATE, FORCE RLS lifted per table inside the transaction) instead of a batched job: tables are small before launch.
  - Package `@inmolink/core` `test:int` now runs with `--testTimeout=30000` like the root projects (part of S1-F1): the first full verify timed out 11 identity tests at the 5 s default.
  - Accepted, not fixed: app_auth UPDATE on `agency_invites` is limited by trigger, not column grants (the RLS generator has no column grants); the sign-up branch of the `agency_members` insert predicate does not check "no members yet" (inside the policy app_auth sees only its own row, so it cannot be expressed); accepting into a SUSPENDED agency creates an account that `withMemberCtx` then refuses; the team page shows the first 100 members/invites (dashboard shell S1-10 adds paging).
